first_impression.reaction: I typed 'corfu wedding venues' on the train and the first sentence tells me the five areas. That's my answer before I've scrolled. The takeaways give me the guest-count range and a heads-up about summer heat, and there's a jump list. I'd read the takeaways, tap Kalami because I've heard of it, look at the weather table, skim the FAQ, then bookmark.

journey.quote: Corfu wedding venues with a sea view sit in five parts of the island: the Kommeno peninsula, Corfu Town and Kanoni, Kalami in the north-east, the south-east coast around Benitses, and Ermones on the west coast.
journey.reaction: Straight answer in line one, matches what I searched. Good.

journey.quote: Guest count narrows the list quickly, because published ceremony spaces run from the couple and eight guests at Atlantica's Secret Garden to 250 at Angsana Corfu's Vertigo Sky Bar.
journey.reaction: Real names, real numbers, smallest to biggest in one line. This is the bit I'd screenshot.

journey.quote: July and August are the driest and hottest months in Corfu, and wildfires occur from June to September, so plan shade, a later ceremony and a covered fallback for a summer date.
journey.reaction: Didn't expect wildfires in a venue list, but that's actually useful. Feels like someone thought about it properly.
Five taps, skip the rest. Exactly what I want on a phone.

journey.section: Corfu wedding venues at a glance
journey.quote: | Venue | Area | Type | Sea view setting | Ceremony options | Largest published capacity | Rooms on site | Exclusive use |
journey.reaction: Eight columns. On my phone I see the venue name and maybe the area, then I'm swiping sideways forever. And half the cells say 'Not published' anyway.

journey.quote: One venue here passes both tests: an adults-only resort on Kalami Bay.
journey.reaction: Which tests? I jumped straight here from the menu, so I have no idea what 'both tests' means. Had to scroll way back up to guess.

journey.quote: Kalami is the village the Durrell family chose as their home while Gerald Durrell wrote his best-known books, and the resort looks straight onto it.
journey.reaction: Oh, that's the Durrells place. Cute detail, makes me want to look it up.

journey.quote: Adults only shapes who can stay on site, so check it against your guest list before you fall for the view.
journey.reaction: Helpful. Tells me who it's not for, which saves me time.

journey.quote: Not published: capacity, ceremony types, exclusive use, curfew.
journey.reaction: Every venue ends on a list of what's missing. Honest, but by the time I've peeked at three of them it feels like the page mostly knows what it doesn't know.

journey.quote: Capacity, ceremony spaces and house rules are not published; your Wedded Advisor confirms them in writing for your date.
journey.reaction: Scrolled up to Kommeno and town and the same 'your Wedded Advisor confirms them in writing' line is there too. Starts to feel like a sales loop.

journey.quote: Its published terms are dated 2023, so ask for current terms.
journey.reaction: Dated and upfront about it. That's exactly my 'is this still true?' question answered.

journey.quote: Outdoor receptions start from 20:30, and outdoor music stops at 23:30, after which the party can move indoors to the main restaurant until 04:00 at the latest.
journey.reaction: Specific times. Love this, it's the kind of thing nobody else tells you.

journey.section: How to compare Corfu venues like for like
journey.quote: Rooms matter more than usual when most guests fly long-haul from Australia.
journey.reaction: Australia again. My guests would be flying from Singapore. Is this written only for Australians?
A tiny table of temps and rain days by month. Quick, scannable, I get it in two seconds.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, Smartraveller says heatwaves are frequent in Greece over the summer months and can cause heat exhaustion and heat stroke; it advises drinking water, wearing a hat and light clothing, and staying in shade or air-conditioning.
journey.reaction: Dated to this month. Good, I know it's current.

journey.quote: Yes. Eva Palace offers "an intimate beach ceremony" on Kommeno Bay, and San Antonio's signature venue, Callao On The Coast, sits on the beach at Kalami.
journey.reaction: Answer in the first word, names in the next sentence. That's how an FAQ should work.

journey.section: Shortlist your Corfu venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: So it is for Australians. Not sure they'd take me.

unanswered_questions: Roughly what does a Corfu venue cost? Even a ballpark. Not one number on the page.
Do you work with couples outside Australia, or only Australians?
Which of these could take around 60 to 80 guests? Most of the venues in the middle of that range don't publish a capacity, so I can't tell.
How do non-Australians handle the legal side? The legal section only covers Australian paperwork.

turn_offs_found.quote: Capacity, ceremony spaces and house rules are not published; your Wedded Advisor confirms them in writing for your date.
turn_offs_found.why: A version of this line closes every area section (Kommeno, Corfu Town, Kalami, the south-east, the west). Once is helpful; five times feels like being sold to while I'm just trying to read about venues.

turn_offs_found.quote: Not published: capacity, ceremony types, exclusive use, curfew.
turn_offs_found.why: All ten venues end on a list of gaps. When I skim on my phone I keep landing on what's missing instead of what's good about the place.

turn_offs_found.quote: | Venue | Area | Type | Sea view setting | Ceremony options | Largest published capacity | Rooms on site | Exclusive use |
turn_offs_found.why: Eight columns doesn't fit a phone screen. I have to swipe sideways to see capacity or exclusive use, and many of those cells are 'Not published', so the swipe often isn't worth it.

turn_offs_found.quote: One venue here passes both tests: an adults-only resort on Kalami Bay.
turn_offs_found.why: I arrived from the jump list, so 'both tests' points at something I never read. The headings are built for jumping, but this line only makes sense if you read from the top.

would_share_with: A friend who's been talking about a Greek island wedding; I'd send her the key takeaways and the weather table

cta_reaction.quote: talk to a Wedded Advisor about your shortlist
cta_reaction.why: I'm just looking, not planning. No pop-ups and the links don't get in the way, so they didn't bother me. I'd bookmark before I'd enquire, and the 'AUD for Australian couples' line makes me think it isn't for me anyway.

top_3_changes: Say the 'your Wedded Advisor confirms them in writing' line once or twice (for example after the comparison section and in the closing), not at the end of every area.

Make each area intro stand on its own for people arriving from the jump list: replace 'One venue here passes both tests' with plain words, such as 'One venue here hosts weddings and states its sea view'.

Trim the 'Not published' lines to the one or two gaps that matter most per venue, and slim the at-a-glance table (fewer columns, or move rooms and exclusive use out) so it reads on a phone without sideways swiping.

assumptions: Persona is provisional (weight 0.10); reactions reflect generic informational search intent.

Arrived from a Google search for 'corfu wedding venues' on a phone; read the intro and takeaways, glanced at the table, used the jump list to reach Kalami, peeked at Kommeno and Corfu Town, then the weather section, FAQ and closing.
Prices are deliberately not printed; the missing ballpark is logged as an unanswered question only.
The Australia-focused framing (AUD, legal section) is logged as a low-severity objection and unanswered question from a non-Australian reader, not a must-fix, since the business focus is deferred.
Read with images not yet loaded; image slots and HTML comments judged as invisible.
Quotes with inline HTML fact comments, link markup or bold markers are given as a reader sees them.
